core_obligations: Assume (1) and derive (2) by unwinding the injectivity of |Y' x_Y X| -> |Y'| through a common field extension of the two residue fields (proof lines 3691-3718).
Assume (2) and derive (1) using the fpqc sheaf property after producing a covering by a field extension on which the two morphisms agree (proof lines 3721-3742).
Assume (3) and derive (2) through the description of points of X x_Y X and the points criterion for surjectivity, using base change stability (proof lines 3745-3755).
Assume (2) and derive (3) by applying injectivity to X x_Y X -> X and converting the resulting surjectivity of |Delta| into surjectivity of Delta (proof lines 3758-3764).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma giving the equivalence of three conditions for a morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over a scheme S: injectivity of X(K) -> Y(K) for every field K over S, injectivity of |Y' x_Y X| -> |Y'| after every base change Y' -> Y, and surjectivity of the diagonal X -> X x_Y X (source lines 3677-3688). Each implication is short but not formal: (1) implies (2) uses field extensions realizing the identification of two points of a fibre product, (2) implies (1) uses the fpqc sheaf property of algebraic spaces, (3) implies (2) uses the points criterion for surjectivity together with the base change stability of condition (3), and (2) implies (3) converts injectivity of |X x_Y X| -> |X| into surjectivity of the diagonal. The four steps together form a genuine cycle and are the reason the notion is usable.
